thread:
maria: Sam in onboarding reported repeated SSE disconnects during long responses. Customer sees partial output, then connection drops and client reconnects but gets duplicate tokens or missing trailing tokens. They said it happens ~1-2x per 100 streams, more on mobile. Logs attached below.

sam: repro steps I used: `curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true\"` — response starts streaming, then after ~30-40s connection closes with `recv() 0` on client. When reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` the model returns repeated tokens for last 3-4 tokens then continues. On mobile the client sees a partial JSON chunk and throws parser error.

maria: thanks. Past issues were ALB / proxy idle timeouts. Can you paste the server logs and the HTTP headers you saw?

sam: headers: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Server logs show stream started, tokens emitted. No explicit close on our app side. Client stacktrace (iOS) shows socket closed by remote.

maria: attached logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-12T14:07:23Z] stream.start request_id=xyz model=gpt-large stream=true
[2026-03-12T14:07:24Z] emit token='The' idx=0
[2026-03-12T14:07:24Z] emit token='quick' idx=1
...
[2026-03-12T14:07:52Z] emit token='fox' idx=47
[2026-03-12T14:07:55Z] connection closed by peer
```

maria: notice connection closed by peer ~31s in. No app error logged.

jason: :eyes: likely a proxy/ALB timeout. Default AWS ALB idle timeout is 60s but some infra components (Cloudflare, nginx) have shorter defaults. But 31s seems suspiciously close to VPC NAT gateway health windows or an internal L7 shim with 30s idle. Also TCP keepalive is not the same as HTTP-level keepalive — OS defaults are way longer (~2h) so it won't help.

priya: theory: our runtime hasn't been emitting SSE comments/pings, so proxies see an idle connection and drop it. Even though tokens stream, perhaps there are long gaps between chunks when model generates long completions and some proxies consider it idle. We should add an application-level heartbeat to ensure at least one byte every N seconds.

sam: what's an app-level heartbeat look like?

priya: for SSE you can send comment lines that clients ignore per spec. Example: `: ping\n\n` sent every 15s. Or send an `event: ping\ndata: {\"t\": 167}\n\n`. Comments are smaller and don't require client parsing. Example SSE chunk (literal in curl):
```
:heartbeat


event: ping
data:  {"ts": 167890}

id: 12345
data: {"text":"partial tokens..."}

```

priya: advantages: comments are spec-compliant, minimal overhead, survive through proxies that are SSE-aware. They also avoid polluting event stream for clients that only parse `data` messages.

jason: important: some middleboxes collapse repeating small packets (TCP Nagle), so we need to ensure chunked flush from app layer (`fflush`/`flush()` depending on runtime) and possibly set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`/`Cache-Control: no-cache`. For nginx we set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\"; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`

maria: action item: propose we implement 2 things: (1) server emits SSE comment ping every 15s when no data has been sent; (2) client reconnection guidance: exponential backoff with jitter, include Last-Event-ID to attempt dedupe/resume, and add a small replay-tolerance window to avoid duplicate tokens.

evan: need to check billing impacts. If we keep sending heartbeats for millions of streams, does this count as tokens? It shouldn't but the transport bytes still count toward egress. We should mark heartbeat bytes as not billable. Current billing logic tallies tokens at model output, not raw bytes, so should be fine, but confirm.

priya: confirms: heartbeats are application-level comments, not produced by the model, so they shouldn't increment token counters. We'll add a metadata flag in logs like `heartbeat_sent=true` to be clear.

jason: also check ALB/nginx idle timeouts: ALB default 60s but HTTP/2 or some edge shims may close after 30s. I'll run a sweep on all frontdoors and list configs. If we can standardize to 90s idle on any proxy layer that would help, but better not to rely on that. App-level heartbeat is safer.

maria: repro playbook for support to confirm fix: 1) Run client that simulates long gaps: `python3 tests/stream_repro.py --delay=20 --count=200` (attached). 2) Without heartbeat the connection should drop ~30s on the customer's infra. 3) With heartbeat enabled the client stays connected. 4) Test reconnect flow: drop socket mid-stream and reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` header to verify resume/dedupe.

priya: sample reconnect/backoff pseudocode for clients:
```
let attempt=0
while (!connected) {
  wait = min(10000, (2**attempt)*100 + random(0,500))
  sleep(wait)
  connect()
  attempt += 1
}
// on reconnect set header: Last-Event-ID: <last-id>
```

sam: for iOS JSON parser errors: recommend clients buffer partial SSE `data:` blocks until `\n\n` terminator. Some mobile libs parse per-line and fail. We'll update our iOS sample client.

maria: nice. priya, can you prototype server comment pings in the runtime and a config toggle (default on for hosted)? jason, check proxies and report back by EOD. evan, confirm billing won't charge for heartbeats. I'll update the support KB and ship repro steps.

priya: will do. planning to implement comment ping every 15s after last token; flush after each comment. Also add config to emit `event: ping` with a sequence id for clients that want explicit events.

jason: running a scan now. found one edge shim with 30s idle — filing infra ticket to raise to 90s for streaming endpoints.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: runtime/stream-heartbeat feature branch -> staging at 2026-03-12T20:00Z.

maria: thanks everyone. Sam, I'll follow up with you once staging deploy lands so you can validate. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround!
